title: 8-round AES-256 impossible-differential key recovery, improved Bahrak-Aref construction

display.name: Impossible differential, BA line, high data

target.description: 8 rounds of standard AES-256 with initial AddRoundKey and final MixColumns omitted. The source reports complete master-key recovery, using impossible-differential subkey elimination followed by key-schedule completion or trial encryption.

setting.key_relation: One fixed unknown AES master key; no related-key oracle.
setting.key_population: general secret key; no weak-key restriction reported
setting.plaintext_model: source-reported chosen-plaintext budget for the improved Bahrak-Aref construction; Appendix B defers detailed structure and candidate-pair generation to the full online version
assumptions: Uses the four-round impossible differential of Proposition 1 with input/output extension and early rejection of wrong key guesses.
Table 1 and Appendix B state 2^227.8 memory accesses, whereas the conclusion states 2^224.3 for the same 2^111.1-data endpoint. Both printed values are retained and numerical normalization is null.

Section 2's textual AES-256 key-schedule description includes a rotation in the i=4 mod 8 branch; the canonical AES specification has an unrotated SubWord there. This source description discrepancy remains flagged for full-version checking; no alternative cipher is silently substituted.

success.description: No numerical finite-budget full-master-key success is established for this exact endpoint. AppendixB gives condensed improvements and explicitly refers the full procedure to the online version. Exact-endpoint wrong-key distribution, repetition accounting and success evidence remain a follow-up task. Its 4/12 output-pattern repetitions are not assumed independent and do not inherit the Phan counter/survival model. Existing resource conflicts remain.
